doc.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Gerald's writing career: Ellington, movies, Philharmonic
summary: Gerald settled in Los Angeles and wrote for Ellington, Al Hirt, movies, TV and the LA Philharmonic, and praises Snooky.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah, it’s a pretty well-told story. When you settled in L.A. later on, you got into some other —
Well I settled in L.A. when I came out here when I left Lunceford’s band. I settled here then and I’ve been here ever since.
And your writing has taken you a lot of different places.

Many different places. I’ve been lucky, I’ve been lucky. I’ve written for practically every band that there was that you can imagine. And my dreams have all been, really, all of my dreams have come true. I wanted to write for people like Duke Ellington. I wrote for Duke and I wrote for him even up until the time he died I was still contributing numbers. I worked, I did two concerts at Carnegie Hall with Al Hirt, and Snooky was on the band then, and J.J. Johnson, we had all those great guys there. And I wanted to write for the movies, and I’ve written for the movies. I wrote for MGM, “Where the Boys Are,” “Love Has Many Faces”; over at Columbia, Ken Murray’s “Hollywood My Home Town.” I’ve

done TV work. Everything I’ve wanted to do. I also wanted to write for the symphony orchestra. And one day I got an invitation to write for the Los Angeles Philharmonic. I composed a number that they performed, and then I later orchestrated six other things for them and Zubin Mehta conducted all of my numbers. So all of my dreams, more or less, have been answered, although I’m still writing today. In fact I was writing yesterday, as my wife can attest to, and I intend to write until I die. I love to write and I love to write things that nobody else has heard before. I believe that I can create, I can write music, I can do it any way I want to now, and so my dreams, like Snooky’s have been answered. Snooky’s the greatest lead trumpet player. I told him he was going to be — by the way — I told him he was going to be the greatest lead trumpet player in the world. And that’s when he said, no, he wasn’t. But I knew he was.
